CMOS clear is currently part of ipmid(maintained as global variable )
https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-host-ipmid/blob/master/chassishandler.cpp#L1848 
Is the plan to use that variable to set the property ?
This variable is not used in the current design; the properties are get and set via OEM IPMI commands.

Hi @patrick@stwcx.xyz,
Could you please help review this Gerrit change?
This change adds the necessary interface and property for the OEM meta command get/set boot order.

I need to know more about the intended implementation here in order to make sure we get appropriate level of feedback.

Someone also previously proposed this: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/78214

Is this one related?

This implementation is unrelated to  https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/78214.

It's intended for the OEM meta IPMI get/set boot order command. 
During system boot, the BIOS issues the get/set boot order command to retrieve the boot order stored in the BMC, and then applies it to configure the boot options.

Here, "CMOS" is a flag indicating whether to clear CMOS, and "bootSequence" represents the boot device order, with values such as "USB_DEV", "NET_IPV6", or "SATA_HDD", etc.

And also, is there any plans from meta to use redfish host interface for boot option, boot order.
There is a design MR in review https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/79327.
Using this bios can GET/POST/PATCH boot order to bmc.

@patrick@stwcx.xyz @prithvi24pai@gmail.com
Hi, if there are any remaining issues after the review, please let me know if anything else needs to be updated. Thanks!

One more thing to consider should we add all the flags under single interface. Example: yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Control/Boot/Flags.interface.yaml

Thank you for your help! I will use this interface for the implementation.

Hi @prithvi24pai@gmail.com

I tried to make the bootOrder property persistent through phosphor-settings (similar to this change https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/openbmc/+/80856), but the build failed.

It seems that when I include the xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Boot.BootOrder interface in the override YAML, the phosphor-settings tries to instantiate the corresponding C++ class. However, because the D-Bus interface YAML defines a method (e.g., CreateBootOption) that is not implemented in the C++ code, the generated class is abstract and cannot be instantiated, causing the build to fail.

Do you have any suggestions?
I will modify this to use the flags interface instead. Thank you!

The backend implementation of this is planned to be done in bios-settings-manager. Do you have any difference of opinion ? Is it okay if its part of bios-settings-manager ? I can share the code in case you are interested.

We are not currently using bios-settings-manager. As we are urgently working to fix the issue, would it be acceptable for us to use our current approach as a short-term solution for now, and further optimize it as part of a long-term solution in the future?
Do you want me to remove the method from the interface ?

Yes, that's fine for me. Then I will just add the Flags interface on my side.

However, could you help merge your changes first? This change https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/openbmc/+/80856 will require the bootOrder property.

Hi @prithvi24pai@gmail.com
I added the bootOrder property mainly for use with the YV4 OEM-meta IPMI command get/set boot order. The BIOS will interact with boot-related properties through IPMI commands to retrieve or configure boot settings. At present, we do not process boot order changes via Redfish; all handling is done through IPMI commands only.
The oem meta command will get or set boot-related properties (such as CMOS clear, boot mode, and boot type...), not just retrieve the boot order property.
@patrick@stwcx.xyz please share your inputs here. As mentioned in above comments meta doesn't use bios-settings-manager. So, what could be the best approach here ?

We should never assume a particular daemon is the only valid implementation of an interface.  I'm not sure what feedback you're looking for from me other than that.  If @zoey.yj.chung.wiwynn@gmail.com has some proposed changes to make this work for their use-case can we incorporate them?

Yes, I completely agree to aim for a common and scalable solution.

The BIOS provides a boot order, which includes a list of various boot options. Each BootOption can contain several additional properties(https://redfish.dmtf.org/schemas/v1/BootOption.v1_0_6.yaml). 
Currently, the approach is to model this interface within phosphor-settingsd. While this may be suitable for static entries like maintaining the overall BootOrder, it may not be the best fit for dynamic or runtime BootOption entries, especially considering scalability. 
Happy to proceed with phosphor-settingsd if that’s considered the best fit.

You're not required to put it in phosphor-settingsd yourself.  If you want to implement in bios-manager for your own platforms, that is fine.  Allowing use in phosphor-settingsd is usually a trivial effort; it is just a YAML update.

Hi @patrick@stwcx.xyz,

We have tried removing the method from this interface (https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/81554) and placing the "BootOrder" property in phosphor-settingsd, and it works as expected.

In that case, for the next step, should we kindly ask @prithvi24pai@gmail.com to remove the method and merge his changes in his Gerrit, or should we proceed to make the changes and merge them in our Gerrit?
81554 isn't going to be acceptable because it uses raw strings.  Can this commit work for your purposes?

Yes, as long as the method in 81554 is removed, we can use it.

Alternatively, if we want to modify this Gerrit to use the enum definition from "Source" interface directly, we may need to add "IPv4", "IPv6", "USB", and "RESERVED" to distinguish between different boot sources in order to meet our requirements. For example, if there is only a "network" option, we would not be able to tell whether it is IPv4 or IPv6.

Do you have any suggestions?
Additionally, our current implementation uses IPMI commands to get/set boot order, following the tables defined in the IPMI specification. We do not use direct string input.

Hi @patrick@stwcx.xyz,
I tried to define a property using array[enum] and attempted to configure it through phosphor-settingsd. However, the current issue is that phosphor-settings doesn't seem to support the array[enum] data type, which results in a build failure.

If that's the case, would it be possible to temporarily use array[string] instead? Alternatively, I might need to store the value persistently using a local file on my side.

Hi @patrick@stwcx.xyz,

I submitted a Gerrit change to phosphor-settingsd to support the array[enum] data type. (https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-settingsd/+/82333)

I also updated the "bootOrder" property here to use array[enum] and added several options to the boot source interface. 

Could you please help review it? If you have any concerns or suggestions for improvement, please let me know!

Thanks!

Hi @zoey.yj.chung.wiwynn@gmail.com
Could this be PDI be part of new file ? 
Having it part of Control/Boot/Source.interface.yaml restricts this to be part of settingsd only. 
I have a use case to implement this as part of biosconfig-manager. 
The reason I think it should be implemented there is as the BootOrder and BootOption changes every boot removing the objects would be difficult as part of settingsd. 
Please share your thoughts.

Hi @prithvi24pai@gmail.com

Would your implementation be able to work with it if I define "BootOrder" as a separate interface (like in https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/81554), register only the property (without registering a method, as that would prevent settingsd from using it), and continue using the current definition of "BootOrder" as an array of enums? I believe using an array[string] approach for "BootOrder" is unlikely to be accepted.

I think if this works, it would allow us to configure the property via settingsd, while still enabling your use case as well.

My use case is BIOS would send us the BootOption via Redfish Host Interface. BMC would form the BootOption object for each bootoptions. 
We required method for this. So I wanted to check with you on this. Do you see any better way of handling this ? If you have any suggestion I would be happy to incorporate it

Hi @prithvi24pai@gmail.com

For our use case, we can store the data in a local file and not add the “BootOrder” property to the PDI. That should allow your side to implement it with your current Gerrit change: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/81554. Would that work for you? How does that sound?

@patrick@stwcx.xyz @zoey.yj.chung.wiwynn@gmail.com 
After reviewing the actual BIOS boot menu structure, I recommend using array[string] as the data structure for representing boot order rather than the current approach. Here's the technical justification:

The current implementation would produce a Redfish boot order representation like
["Default", "Disk", "Disk", "Disk"...]

This generic categorization fails to provide meaningful boot order information to clients consuming the Redfish API.

Using array[string] would enable accurate representation:
[ "Ubuntu", "DGX OS",... ]

This information is going to be bi-directional?  From the BIOS and from the user?  Or is it just from the user?

We generally prohibit arbitrary strings because we do not have a way to confirm correctness.  If you allow a user to put in an arbitrary string over Redfish, we have to accept it (return success) but then it fails later on when they try to actually boot their system.  This isn't a great experience.

If we get a set of all the valid options from the BIOS, save that, and only allow users to set ones from a "valid options list" this seems more reasonable.

Alternatively, I think you could use some kind of position identifier in addition to "Disk" or "Network".  The UEFI BootOrder variable is numbered (something like "Boot0001" by my recollection).

Hi @prithvi24pai@gmail.com

I've verified the updated change (https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/81554) on our platform, and it meets our requirements. 

I will remove the "bootorder" property from this Gerrit and retain only the "flags" part. 

Thanks!

Who is going to implement this interface?  Is this something that is typically sent to the BIOS and we should put this in bios-settings-manager or is this something for phosphor-state-manager?  I don't really know and there isn't any design here.  I'd like to get the right people to give feedback on this.
This flag is usually used in `chassis bootparam get 5`. BIOS can directly send this command to GET/SET this param. phosphor-settings-manager can have this. Is there any other thoughts ?

One more thing to consider should we add all the flags under single interface. Example: `yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Control/Boot/Flags.interface.yaml`
All the flags coming in future could go to same interface
Arbitrary strings are not likely to be acceptable here.  We have the "Sources" below as an enumeration.  How is "Boot Source" and "Boot Sequence" different?

Currently boot source is implemented as part of phosphor-settings-manager. The boot sequence is obtained from bios run time which is dynamic in nature. And also user has the option to delete the boot option(single option in the sequence). How does settings-manager delete the option ? Should boot option be a separate interface ?

The current implementation uses the OEM-meta IPMI command get/set boot order to set the value of the boot sequence. 
The current approach replaces boot options with the value "RESERVED". 
For example, the sequence changes from {"USB_DEV", "NET_IPV6", "SATA_HDD", "SATA_CD", "RESERVED"} to {"USB_DEV", "NET_IPV6", "RESERVED", "RESERVED", "RESERVED"}.
Do you have any suggestions?

At what point are we clearing the `RESERVED` ? 
Is this data reflected as part of redfish/v1/Systems/<system-id> ?

As of now, "RESERVED" entries are not cleared. If an entry in the boot sequence is set to "RESERVED", the corresponding byte in the response data will be returned as 0xFF.

Currently, this is not reflected under redfish/v1/Systems/<system-id>. These properties are only used by OEM IPMI commands in YV4.

How does pending boot order retrieved ?
BIOS can send the boot order which is CurrentBootOrder. Users can set the boot order which can be PendingBootOrder ? 
So I think we could re-use this PDI https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/78214/5/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Control/Boot/BootOrder.interface.yaml

This is still pending feedback.  I'm not allowing arbitrary strings here, especially when we have `Sources` already enumerated.

If we need to add RESERVED fields, add them?  Strings are problematic because users never know if they were correct.
@deepak.kodihalli.83@gmail.com @rohitpai77@gmail.com please share your inputs

Would your implementation be able to work with it if I define "BootOrder" as a separate interface (like in https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/81554), register only the property (without registering a method, as that would prevent settingsd from using it), and continue using the current definition of "BootOrder" as an array of enums?
